institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 20, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2013. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published April 2014.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in pie-chart legends and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2012 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (sgrhgrid2.py: pdfplumber word positions, run with the pdfminer inline-image patch; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU from each row's background colour and checked against the row order; organism labels assigned by vertical position, the blood GNB table printing Acinetobacter before P. aeruginosa), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. The one row with fewer values than headers (blood GPC S. aureus ICU) was read on the image: its Ampicillin cell is printed empty. Organism pie charts (no data labels): legend and "others" entries were re-parsed from the text layer inside each panel box (the page-thirds split of counts.py cut the first letters of ICU "others" names and split names across lines), checked per panel (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates and the "others" entries sum to Others: all 15 panels balance) and every entry was compared by eye with the charts rendered at scale 5. Second reader 2026-09-26: see issues.

notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 20, No. 1 (published April 2014), data January to December 2013, 8 pages; the layout of the 2011 and 2012 editions (organism pie charts). Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism pie charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list; figures in parentheses are repeat isolates, excluded from the data) and GPC and GNB percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus wound swab"), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci (the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)"). Combined columns: "Cefoxitin / Oxacillin" (every GPC table) is recorded under oxacillin (for blood S. pneumoniae the cell note says so without the methicillin wording), "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) under meropenem and "Glycopeptide" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure), each cell noted; the "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid and chloramphenicol (recorded). Compared with 2012 the blood GNB table has no Enterobacter row and prints Acinetobacter before P. aeruginosa, the urine GNB table adds Acinetobacter and the respiratory GNB table adds Haemophilus influenzae; every table was mapped by its own headers and labels. The blood GPC S. aureus ICU row prints its Ampicillin cell empty (no value, no dash; noted on the row). Blood S. Typhi Quinolones are printed "4*" (OPD) and "6*" (ward) with the footnote "Decrease in Quinolone susceptibility in S. typhi is due to implementation of new CLSI cut off"; page 8 explains that the ciprofloxacin susceptible cut-off changed from 1 to 0.06 microgram/ml (CLSI M100-S22, 2012), raising ciprofloxacin resistance in Salmonella from 24.3% (2012) to 93.7% (2013). The Quinolones column is not recorded. Every page states: "All sensitivities reported here are based on MIC testing using Vitek - 2 according to 2012 CLSI guidelines". Isolate numbers: every tabulated organism equals its chart entry, and all 15 panels balance (legend plus Others equals Isolates; the "others" list sums to Others). No printed percentage is flagged by the arithmetic check against the row's n. Printed values the build treats as intrinsic resistance (noted on the cells): Klebsiella ampicillin 0 in every specimen, Acinetobacter aztreonam in every specimen, urine Proteus nitrofurantoin 0. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Morganii spp." as Morganella spp., "Serratia marscecens", "Elizebethkingia", "S. maltophila"); entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. "Salmonella typhimurium" and "Salmonella entertidis" are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella, and "Group A Streptococcus" and "Streptococcus pyogenes Group A" both as S. pyogenes (blood ICU prints both, 1 and 2). S. maltophilia is printed twice in the respiratory ICU panel (legend 48 and "others" "S. maltophila-1"); both recorded as printed. This edition names the fungi "Candida spp." in the legends and "others" lists (the 2012 and 2014 charts say "Fungal isolates"); Candida spp., Candida albicans (respiratory OPD 1) and Cryptococcus neoformans (blood ICU 2) have organism keys and are recorded; their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Page 1 and 8: new IAMM-EQAS centre, book release, conferences, publications, visitors, reflections, faculty and a highlights box; page 7: antimicrobial consumption (DDD per 100 bed days) and the Drug Resistance Index trend 2009 to 2013. Source: https://sgrh.com/en/publications, Microbiology Newsletter selector, issue "April-2014"; the site serves the PDF only by an HTTP POST from that selector (downloaded file name mb-april2014.pdf), so no direct PDF URL exists.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,087 cells, all 109 row n values and all 281 organism counts checked against the PDF (pdfplumber run with the SGRH pyfix patch): every table, the seeded 25% sample of 272 cells from sample_cells.py included, was read from the page images and transcribed (tables at scale 3.2 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept; chart panels at scale 5) before comparing with the extraction, and every cell, row n, row fill colour, row label and column header was also compared with an independent parse of the text layer written for this check (values clustered by row and column, rotated header text per column, labels by vertical position, row fill sampled from the rendered page).

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 272; whole file 0 of 1,087 cells, 0 of 109 n, 0 of 281 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink row fills as the colour key, always in OPD, ward, ICU order); the organism label of every row triple is correct; every printed value of a recorded column is in the file; the 8 printed rows not recorded are exactly the 8 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% threshold.

Column headers: every table was mapped by its own headers and labels (the blood GNB table prints Acinetobacter before P. aeruginosa and has no Enterobacter row). Cefoxitin / Oxacillin (25 cells, the 3 blood S. pneumoniae cells noted without the methicillin wording) under oxacillin, Imipenem / Meropenem (64 cells) under meropenem and Glycopeptide (40 cells) under vancomycin each carry the combined-column cell note; High Dose Gentamicin (9 cells) is under gentamicin_hl. Body fluid OPD E. coli prints "-" under Imipenem / Meropenem (not recorded; ertapenem 80 is).

Confirmed on the page: the blood GPC S. aureus ICU Ampicillin cell is printed empty (no value, no dash), not recorded and noted on the row; blood S. Typhi Quinolones "4*" (OPD) and "6*" (ward) with the footnote "*Decrease in Quinolone susceptibility in S. typhi is due to implementation of new CLSI cut off. (Refer highlights on page 8 of this newsletter)"; the Quinolones column is not recorded and the footnote and the page 8 explanation are in notes and excluded.

Charts: all 15 pie panels re-read from the images; every legend and "others" entry agrees with counts or excluded, every panel balances (legend counts plus Others equal Isolates; the "others" list sums to Others) and every tabulated organism equals its chart entry. "Candida spp." is each panel's whole fungal entry: no 2013 panel prints an unnamed "Fungal isolates" entry, the only other fungi named are blood ICU Cryptococcus neoformans 2 and respiratory OPD Candida albicans 1 (that panel's only fungal entry), and respiratory ward prints none, so recording them as counts is correct.

Cells not kept: the 32 intrinsic cells (Klebsiella ampicillin 0 in every specimen, Acinetobacter aztreonam in every specimen, urine Proteus nitrofurantoin 0) are printed that way, not transcription errors. No caution cells and no count mismatches.
